release_state.pre_1_0_rule: Compiler 0.y releases may change the experimental compiler surface with a minor bump, but an AxiOM-owned surface explicitly marked stable still follows stable-surface SemVer and deprecation rules.

stable.requirements: A stable signature change or removal requires a major bump and migration; an addition requires a minor bump; a compatible correction requires a patch bump.

experimental.requirements: Experimental drift carries no backward-compatibility promise, but every semantic change must increase its surface version and remain visible in the report.

deprecated.requirements: A deprecated surface keeps its last stable signature through the full deprecation window; deprecation itself requires a minor bump, migration, and semantic replacement.

editions.implementation_status: The current manifest and compiler do not expose an edition selector; 2026 is a policy identifier for future migration qualification, not a selectable released language edition.

previous_supported.reason: No immutable AxiOM compiler tag or published compiler release exists, so there is no previous supported compiler to qualify yet.

language.identity: AxiOM syntax, type, ownership, effect, diagnostic, and edition semantics identified by AxiOM semantic names.
language.additive: A syntax or semantic addition is additive only when existing programs keep the same meaning; a stable addition requires a minor bump.
language.breaking: A changed parse, type, ownership, effect, diagnostic, or runtime meaning requires a major bump and migration when stable.

stdlib.identity: AxiOM module IDs and semantic function signatures from the governed stdlib catalog.
stdlib.additive: New modules or functions are additive; stable additions require a minor surface bump.
stdlib.breaking: Removal or semantic signature change of a stable item requires deprecation, a major bump, and a migration.

cli.identity: Command names, documented flags, exit behavior, and versioned AxiOM JSON envelopes.
cli.additive: New optional flags or commands are additive and require a minor surface bump when stable.
cli.breaking: Removing or changing a stable command, flag, exit meaning, or JSON field requires a major bump and migration.
cli.machine_output: Only versioned JSON selected by --json is a stable machine contract; producers follow schema producer rules and consumers follow schema consumer rules.
cli.human_output: Human-readable text, help wrapping, progress, and diagnostic prose are not byte-stable contracts; documented command names, flags, exit meaning, and diagnostic codes remain governed.

package_manifest.identity: The axiom.toml semantic field model identified by its published schema.
package_manifest.additive: Optional fields are additive; newly required fields are breaking.
package_manifest.breaking: Removing fields, tightening accepted values, or changing field meaning requires a major bump and migration.

lockfile.identity: The numeric axiom.lock format version and semantic package records.
lockfile.additive: Readers may accept a new optional field without changing the format version.
lockfile.breaking: An incompatible encoding or required field increments the numeric format version and requires regeneration guidance.

schema.identity: Published AxiOM schema IDs and semantic fields, never serializer or host-language type names.
schema.additive: Optional fields and new variants are additive only when older consumers remain valid.
schema.breaking: Required fields, removed variants, or changed meanings require a new schema ID or major surface bump.
schema.producer_compatibility: A producer may add only schema-permitted optional fields under the same version and must continue emitting all fields required by supported consumers.
schema.consumer_compatibility: A consumer must accept schema-permitted optional additions but must reject unknown fields when the published schema has additionalProperties false and reject unsupported schema versions.

abi.identity: AxiOM target, value, capability, and process-status semantics.
abi.additive: New supported semantic rows are additive; partial rows remain experimental.
abi.breaking: Changing a stable value, capability, or process-status contract requires a major bump and migration.
abi.physical_layout: Rust types, enum discriminants, repr attributes, serializer layout, crate paths, and native host layout are implementation details and forbidden from the public ABI contract.

artifact.identity: AxiOM artifact envelope schema, semantic artifact kind, and provenance IDs.
artifact.additive: New artifact kinds or optional envelope fields are additive.
artifact.breaking: Changing required envelope meaning or removing a stable kind requires a major bump and migration.
